A release you can use

Guion 0.9.1 is out for Linux (Debian 12 on ARM64 and x86_64), macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows (x86_64). It has a written stability policy, a live package registry, native arrays, closures, enums, generic functions, an editor server, and a web package with sessions, CSRF protection and checked templates. Both Mac builds are signed and notarized by Apple, so they open without a warning; the first launch checks with Apple and needs an internet connection. The Windows build is not signed, so Windows may warn the first time it runs, and the Intel Mac and Windows builds have had a build and a short smoke test, not the full test suite. Guion is still pre-1.0, and Python is a released language with a long track record.

Each archive on the release page has a matching SHA-256 checksum file. On macOS and Linux, brew install rmichaelthomas/guion/guion and a one-line installer script also work.
